title: Add documentation on HEALPix extension to ellipsoids
body:
PR to add a new documentation page describing how to extend the HEALPix pixelation to an ellipsoid.

### What's included
- `ellipsoidal-extension.md`: explains the area-preserving transformation from ellipsoid to authalic sphere.
- `elliposid_schema.png`: illustration of the mapping process.
- Link to the new page added in `docs/healpix/index.md`.

### Motivation
Standard HEALPix assumes a spherical Earth. This extension enables its use on ellipsoidal models (e.g., WGS84) while preserving its key properties: equal area, isolatitude, and hierarchy.

### TODO
- add a link to `ellipsoidal-extension.md` in `docs/healpix/reference-system.md` when added to the doc. 

@keewis feel free to review!

+# HEALPix Extension to Ellipsoids
+
+This page outlines an extension of the HEALPix pixelation scheme to ellipsoidal Earth models using an **authalic transformation**-a mapping to a sphere that preserves surface area.
+
+```{figure} ellipsoid_schema.png
+Ellipsoidal to Authalic Mapping
+```
+
+## Why Extend HEALPix?
+
+Standard HEALPix is defined on the sphere and provides:
+
+- Hierarchical structure
+- Isolatitude grid
+- Equal-area pixels
+
+However, many geospatial applications use **ellipsoidal models** (e.g. WGS84). To maintain HEALPix's properties on an ellipsoid, it is mapped to an **authalic sphere**-a sphere with the same surface area.
+
+## Overview
+
+1. **Authalic Mapping**
+   Geodetic latitudes ($\phi$) on the ellipsoid are mapped to authalic latitudes ($\xi$) on the sphere via an area-preserving transformation.
+
+2. **HEALPix on the Sphere**
+   Standard HEALPix is applied on the (authalic) sphere using latitude $\xi$ and longitude $\lambda$.
+
+3. **Optional Reverse Mapping**
+   Pixel centers or boundaries can be projected back to ellipsoidal coordinates if needed.
+
+Authalic mappings:
+
+- Forward: $\phi \to \xi$ (ellipsoid $\to$ sphere)
+- Reverse: $\xi \to \phi$ (sphere $\to$ ellipsoid)
+
+## Ellipsoidal Pixelation
+
+This method results in an **distorted HEALPix grid** on the ellipsoid, preserving equal-area properties. It is ideal for satellite data, climate grids, and DGGS applications that need to account for Earth's flattening.
+
+## See Also
+
+- 📄 [Reference System – HEALPix-Geo Documentation](../reference-system.md)

ground_truth.body: after searching for that, I found a reference to the "equiareal map" in differential geometry, which works for any kind of surface. With that, your sentence makes much more sense, but I think we can make it a lot less confusing. Linking to a description of the differential geometry term elsewhere could be one way to make the intention much clearer, but I think we can also make the sentence easier to understand that way.

other_rounds.body:
Not sure if this fits, but I'd use

```suggestion
However, many geospatial applications require **ellipsoidal models** (e.g. WGS84). As a consequence, to be viable for these HEALPix needs to be mapped to ellipsoids of revolution.
```

(note, "ellipsoid of revolution" is intentional, as there are "triaxial ellipsoids" that we want to exclude here)
